correctness.rationale: The induced map π_K:K(X)→K(Y), C↦π(C), is continuous for the Hausdorff/Vietoris topology, onto because π(π^(−1)(B))=B for each nonempty compact B⊂Y, and G-equivariant. Any G-invariant η on K(Y) admits a probability lift λ_0 on K(X) by compactness/surjectivity; amenability gives a G-invariant lift via convex averaging over a Følner/Reiter net (or the amenable fixed-point theorem), preserving the η pushforward at every step. Since λ is concentrated on K_G(X)∪{X}, and the generalized K_G(X) consists of finite unions of compact central orbit segments ∪_{x∈F}{g x:g∈I_x} with I_x compact in Z(G), equivariance takes each such set to the same finite union of central orbit segments in Y; π_K(X)=Y. Therefore η is concentrated on K_G(Y)∪{Y}. This proves the one-way permanence for all lcsc amenable acting groups, nondiagonal actions and possible infinite fibers. Følner sequence is not necessary to assert if amenability is formulated through invariant means and Reiter nets; the compact fixed-point construction is valid. The proof does not identify or classify actual nontrivial flow factors.
residual_risks: Only amenable acting groups (or others with invariant probability lifting), not arbitrary nonamenable groups.
Non-discrete central orbit segments can be infinite; disjoint central segments/fibers are not assumed.
The claim says factors inherit, never converse or existence of a nontrivial horocycle factor.

originality.rationale: The precise discrete-group factor-permanence theorem is already in Kra–Schmieding Proposition 3.4/§3.3, so the method of invariant-measure lifting is NOT new. Kanigowski–Kasprzak–Lorenzo-Laguno Definition 2.8 genuinely changes the allowable compact sets from finite sets to finite unions of compact central orbit segments and Theorem C provides non-discrete horocycle examples; their displayed definition does not state a corresponding factor theorem. Equivariant images preserve those central orbit-segment classes, an additional compatibility fact that does not follow from the discrete statement by merely declaring all compacts finite. No checked paper states this generalized factor permanence, though the proof is a short adaptation of prior ideas.
residual_risks: It is a formally natural extension of the earlier discrete factor theorem, with limited proof complexity; another author might regard the compatibility as implicit.
The exact new K_G definition could be accompanied by an unstated but immediate functoriality observation in follow-up notes.

value.rationale: Factor stability is a natural structural permanence question for the newly enlarged IC-rigidity of non-discrete actions; it determines how the original horocycle examples behave under compact-metric topological quotients. Even though the proof recycles the amenable hyperspace-lifting method from the discrete theory, the precise central compact-orbit-segment image closure is the required new compatibility check. This is a small but reusable mathematical lemma, not merely a title change; no general classification or new flow construction is claimed.
residual_risks: Very short adaptation; mathematical depth modest, and value depends on utility of factor permanence for genuinely non-discrete examples.
If a published general abstract hereditary class theorem includes this class automatically, value and originality would need re-evaluation.
